correctness.rationale: The three regular differentials have the indicated basis; x and y have pole orders 3 and 4 at infinity, and the finite branch points cause no poles. In characteristic seven, y^(−j)=f^(2j)y^(−7j) yields the coefficient matrix whose seventh roots represent the inverse-Frobenius-semilinear operator. Independent multinomial extraction and a resultant give the displayed entries, discriminant, and 3 det(B)=aΔ. Rank zero for B would imply b=0,c=2a² and Δ=0. At a=0, B=uv, and raising the twice-composed map to 49th powers gives B^(7)B; this vanishes exactly when v^(7)u=−3c(c³−2b⁴)(c³+2b⁴) vanishes. Smoothness removes the last factor; otherwise the rank-one image stays nonzero under further compositions. In the two zero-rank branches b is nonzero, and normalizing b to 1 plus residual cube-root scalings gives one orbit per branch. The branches are disjoint open and closed in the smooth rank-zero locus by the regular invariant c³/b⁴. The nonzero branch is isomorphic to G_m via b=s³,c=ρs⁴ with inverse s=c/(ρb), so it is irreducible as asserted. The separate F_7 check gave Cartier/stable rank counts (1,0):12, (1,1):30, (3,3):252; the symbolic proof covers the algebraic closure.
residual_risks: No unmarked isomorphism classification or full Newton-polygon/Ekedahl–Oort classification is inferred. The rational census is only a check of the algebraic proof.
